entries.text: N, P and K are the three main nutrients plants need in large amounts: Nitrogen (N) for leafy growth, Phosphorus (P) for roots and flowering, and Potassium (K) for overall plant strength and disease resistance.
OC (organic carbon) is a measure of organic matter in the soil; higher OC generally means healthier, more fertile soil that holds water and nutrients better.

pH measures how acidic or alkaline the soil is, on a scale where 7 is neutral; most crops grow best in a range of about 6 to 7.5, and pH outside that range can lock up nutrients even if they are present in the soil.
Nutrient-use efficiency (NUE) is the share of applied nutrient the crop is actually likely to take up and use, rather than lose to the environment; a higher NUE means less waste for the same dose.

The confidence score is a rough, honest indicator of how much to trust a specific estimate - based on things like whether your inputs came from a lab report, how well weather and soil signals agreed, and how typical your values are - it is not a guarantee.
The sustainability score blends nutrient-use efficiency, estimated emissions and nutrient surplus into one number out of 100, to give a quick sense of how environmentally sound a fertilizer plan is.
